news.title: Jonas Urbig grateful about his World Cup experience
news.lede: Jonas Urbig is a name that is quickly becoming a hot topic in German football. Hailed as the next replacement for Manuel Neuer (after Alexander Nübel ultimately fell short), Urbig has had some memorable performances over the last year, and impressed enough for Julian Nagelsmann to send him overseas to join Die Mannschaft as part of the practice squad for the World Cup. “We were all knocked out together; I was part of the group. Even so, it was an incredible experience for me; I got a taste of tournament life and learnt a lot,” said a bittersweet Urbig looking back on the World Cup this summer, as captured by @iMiaSanMia.

news.title: Grant Johnson revelations raise questions over Bafana Bafana’s World Cup camp
news.lede: Former Bafana Bafana goalkeeper coach Grant Johnson has lifted the lid on some of his experiences with the national team, suggesting that not everything behind the scenes before and during the 2026 FIFA World Cup went as smoothly as it appeared from the outside. Johnson, who was part of Hugo Broos’ technical team at the World Cup, made the revelations during an appearance on Peter du Toit’s Soccer Beat podcast. His comments have sparked debate among South African football supporters, particularly around the administration and logistical preparation of the national team. According to Johnson, some of the problems experienced by the team were outside the control of the South African Football Association (SAFA), while others, in his view, could have been prevented.

news.title: Qatar still not satisfied with Asia chief over Infantino letter
news.lede: Aug 20 - The Qatar Football Association has reiterated its concerns over the lack of consultation with members before the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) signed an open letter with UEFA and CONCACAF criticising FIFA President Gianni Infantino. Infantino, who is seeking reelection next year, has faced open revolt after the letter attacked his conduct over the aborted bid to bring private investment into the World Cup and called into question his leadership. In the third letter in a testy exchange, all of which have been seen by Reuters, QFA President Hamad bin Khalifa Al-Thani, an Infantino loyalist, said the AFC's response to his original complaint "raised considerably more questions than it answers".

news.title: Former England international thinks Argentina World Cup loss could open Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane
news.lede: Former England international Danny Mills believes Harry Kane deserves serious consideration in the Ballon d’Or conversation after another phenomenal year for club and country. “Looking at the Ballon d’Or, Harry Kane has probably been the most consistent player in football so far this year. He’s been phenomenal, but I don’t think there’s been one particularly shining light; it undoubtedly depends on who is voting. I’m sure even though the final didn’t go to plan, Lionel Messi will get a few votes,” Mills told talkSPORT Bet slots site.

news.title: K League 1 champions Jeonbuk stunned at top nat'l football tournament
news.lede: Defending league and cup champions Jeonbuk Hyundai Motors fell to Dangjin Citizen on penalties in the round of 16. The reigning Korean football league champions, Jeonbuk Hyundai Motors, suffered a massive upset in their first knockout match of the top national football tournament on Wednesday. Jeonbuk, the 2025 K League 1 champions, lost to third-division club Dangjin Citizen 5-3 on penalties in the round of 16 at the Korea Cup at Jeonju World Cup Stadium in Jeonju, North Jeolla. Jeonbuk, who also won the 2025 Korea Cup for a domestic double, are tied with Pohang Steelers for the most Korea Cup titles with six apiece but will not have a chance to add to their total this year.
